senses.definition: (physical) An area; somewhere within an area.

subsenses.definition: An open space, particularly a city square, market square, or courtyard.

quotes.text: Ay, sir, the other squirrel was stolen from me by the hangman's boys in the market-place

subsenses.definition: (often in street names or addresses) A street, sometimes but not always surrounding a public place, square, or plaza of the same name.
examples: They live at Westminster Place.

subsenses.definition: An inhabited area: a village, town, or city.
Any area of the earth: a region.
examples: He is going back to his native place on vacation.

subsenses.definition: The area one occupies, particularly somewhere to sit.
examples: We asked the restaurant to give us a table with three places.

subsenses.definition: The area where one lives: one's home, formerly (chiefly) country estates and farms.
examples: Do you want to come over to my place later?

quotes.text: My Lady Dedlock has been down at what she calls, in familiar conversation, her "place" in Lincolnshire.

subsenses.definition: An area of the body, especially the skin.
examples: Which place hurts the most?

subsenses.definition: (euphemistic slang) An area to urinate and defecate: an outhouse or lavatory.

senses.definition: A particular location in a book or document, particularly the current location of a reader
examples: I lost my place when you interrupted me.

senses.definition: (obsolete) A passage or extract from a book or document.
(obsolete, rhetoric) A topic.
A state of mind.
examples: I'm in a strange place at the moment.

senses.definition: (chess, obsolete) A chess position; a square of the chessboard.
(social) A responsibility or position in an organization.

subsenses.definition: A role or purpose; a station.
examples: It is really not my place to say what is right and wrong in this case.

quotes.text: I know my place as I would they should do theirs.

subsenses.definition: The position of a contestant in a competition.
examples: We thought we would win but only ended up in fourth place.

subsenses.definition: (horse racing) The position of first, second, or third at the finish, especially the second position.
examples: to win a bet on a horse for place

subsenses.definition: The position as a member of a sports team.
examples: He lost his place in the national team.

senses.definition: (obsolete) A fortified position: a fortress, citadel, or walled town.
Numerically, the column counting a certain quantity.
examples: three decimal places;  the hundreds place

senses.definition: Ordinal relation; position in the order of proceeding.
examples: That's what I said in the first place!

a. 1788, Mather Byles, quoted in The Life of James Otis by William Tudor
In the first place, I do not understand politics; in the second place, you all do, every man and mother's son of you; in the third place, you have politics all the week, pray let one day in the seven be devoted to religion […]

senses.definition: Reception; effect; implying the making room for.

quotes.text: My word hath no place in you.

examples: He placed the glass on the table.
to place someone on a pedestal

senses.definition: (ergative) To earn a given spot in a competition; to rank at a certain position ((often followed by an ordinal)).
examples: The Cowboys placed third in the league.
Run Ragged was placed fourth in the race.

subsenses.definition: (intransitive, motor racing) To finish second, especially of horses or dogs.
examples: In the third race: Aces Up won, paying eight dollars; Blarney Stone placed, paying three dollars; and Cinnamon showed, paying five dollars.

senses.definition: (transitive) To remember where and when (an object or person) has been previously encountered.
examples: I've seen him before, but I can't quite place where.

senses.definition: (transitive) To vouch for someone's alibi.
examples: The librarian was placed at home by her neighbor at the time of the murder.

senses.definition: (transitive) To sing (a note) with the correct pitch.
(transitive, in collocations) To make.
examples: to place a call
to place an order
to place an ad in the newspaper
to place a bid
to place a bet
to place a wager

senses.definition: (transitive) To bet.

senses.definition: (transitive) To recruit or match an appropriate person for a job, or a home for an animal for adoption, etc.
examples: They phoned hoping to place her in the management team.
